# Copilot instructions

This repository contains nixos configuration for multiple hosts / users. It uses the denful framework https://den.denful.dev/.

## Build, test, and lint commands

- Build and run the generated VM for the current host: `nix run .#vm-<hostname>`
- Run the full check suite used by CI: `nix flake check`
- Format the repo with treefmt: `nix fmt`
- After changing `flake-file.inputs` or flake wiring, regenerate the generated flake: `nix run .#write-flake`
- Never switch to the new nixos configuration.

## High-level architecture

- `flake.nix` is generated by `flake-file` and should be treated as derived output. It delegates outputs to `inputs.import-tree ./modules`, so the real source of truth is the module tree plus `outputs.nix`.
- `modules/default.nix` and `modules/dendritic.nix` bootstrap the flake-file/den integration and shared inputs. Modules can declare their own `flake-file.inputs`; those declarations are folded into the generated root flake.
- `modules/hosts.nix` is the inventory and routing entrypoint. It declares hosts and attached users, and enables the den policy that routes the host graph into flake-parts outputs. The current live host is `x86_64-linux.ardell` with users `arnaud` and `guest`.
- Host- and user-specific behavior is composed from aspects under `modules/hosts/*.nix` and `modules/users/*.nix`, not from one monolithic machine file.
  - Host aspects define NixOS config and can push default Home Manager config to attached users through `provides.to-users.homeManager`.
  - User aspects define user creation plus Home Manager config and can push NixOS fragments back to any host that includes them through `provides.to-hosts.nixos`.
- `modules/nh.nix` exposes host/home build targets as flake packages, which is why the normal workflow is `nix run .#<host>` instead of calling `nh` directly.
- `modules/vm.nix` derives `vm-<host>` packages from `inputs.self.nixosConfigurations`, so VM entrypoints are generated automatically from the host inventory.
- `modules/classes/treefmt.nix` routes a custom `treefmt` class into flake-parts, and `modules/fmt.nix` configures formatter exclusions and disables `deadnix` and `nixf-diagnose`.

## Key conventions

- Prefer editing files under `modules/`; do not hand-edit `flake.nix`.
- When a module needs a new flake input, add it via that module's `flake-file.inputs` and then regenerate the flake with `nix run .#write-flake`.
- Extend behavior by composing den aspects, classes, and policies instead of centralizing changes in `modules/hosts.nix`. Use `modules/hosts.nix` for inventory/wiring, and keep actual behavior in the per-host or per-user aspect files.
- Shared defaults live in `modules/defaults.nix`, including the default `homeManager` user class and the NixOS/Home Manager `stateVersion` values.
- Use `modules/hosts.nix` and `nix flake show --all-systems` as the authoritative source for current host names and exported app names.
